newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan militia leader says took towns from rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sudan militia leader says took towns from rebels.

text.p: The commander of a militia allied with the Sudanese government said his forces helped recapture five southern towns from rebels, a Khartoum newspaper reported on Sunday.

"Our forces recaptured more than five towns on their way to the town of Tonj," the independent Akhbar al-Youm quoted Riek Machar as saying. He named Warap, Lirna, Makoj, Tashawi and Tali, and said they were in government hands early on Saturday.
Machar is the commander of the Southern Sudan Defence Force (SSDF), the unified force of a number of factions which signed a peace accord with the Islamist government in April.
Machar did not give a time but the private Sudanese Alwan newspaper said last week that the SSDF on Tuesday retook Warap and Tali, more than 960 km (600 miles) south of Khartoum.
He said the government and SSDF forces took the towns from the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) of John Garang.
Machar "wondered why Garang should reject a ceasefire when nobody asked for one," the newspaper reported in an apparent reference to remarks by made by Garang on Saturday.

Garang had told Reuters in Nairobi that he had rejected a ceasefire request by Sudan. He said Sudan President Lt-General Omar Hassan Al-Bashir's request for a ceasefire was conveyed to regional heads of state at a summit in Nairobi last week.
Garang said his forces, allied with exiled northern rebels, had made gains in the latest fighting. On Monday, Garang said his forces were encircling Juba, capital of the war-torn south.

Sudan's First Vice President Lt-Gen Al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh on Thursday flew to Juba, where he told members of the Popular Defence Force, a militia formed in 1989 to help the army crush the SPLA, that government forces were determined to liberate every inch of Sudan.
For 14 years the government has been fighting the SPLA, which wants greater autonomy or independence for the mostly Christian and animist south from the Moslem Arabised north.
